previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A male patient with a history of atrial fibrillation, aortic stenosis, chronic diastolic heart failure, and spinal stenosis was admitted due to altered mental status. He had recently started a fentanyl patch for back pain and had not had a bowel movement in several days. The confusion was attributed to toxic encephalopathy likely caused by the fentanyl, with possible contribution from constipation and mild fluid overload from heart failure. The fentanyl patch was discontinued, a bowel regimen was initiated, and the furosemide dose was increased to 20 mg daily. The patient improved rapidly, regained full orientation, and was discharged to extended care with instructions to avoid fentanyl, continue current pain medications, monitor INR weekly, and discuss starting an ACE inhibitor with his cardiologist.

ACTIVE ISSUES BY PROBLEM: # Acute on chronic diastolic CHF: initial presenting symptom of shortness of breath attributed to volume overload and resultant pleural effusions from his diastolic CHF and aortic stenosis. He was diuresed with IV lasix initially, with some improvement in exam and symptoms. Interventional pulmonary was consulted for thoracentesis, which successfully drained 1L of fluid from right pleural space with further improvement in symptoms (see below). He was transitioned back to his home dose of lasix 20mg PO daily and constinued on aspirin and metoprolol. He is not on an ACEI for unclear reasons, would defer to PCP to consider starting this as an outpatient. If he does experience worsening shortness of breath again, ___ at the ___ Cardiology Clinic at ___ should be contacted at ___. # Pleural effusions: likely a major contributor to his shortness of breath. Initially covered empirically for PNA, however CXR and symptoms are not convincing for pulmonary infection. IP performed thoracentesis with improvement in symptoms, fluid consistent with transudate, likely from CHF. Fluid cytology negative for malignancy. Unfortunately, he will likely experience reaccumulation of his fluid at some point in the future given his significan CHF and valvular disease. If he does experience worsening shortness of breath again, ___ ___ at the ___ Cardiology Clinic at ___ should be contacted at ___. Overall improved, able to ambulate to bathroom well. # Cellulitis: RLE ultrasound negative x2 for DVT, also had CTA of RLE to assess for arterial thrombus, which did not show any clot. Started IV vancomycin initially with some improvement, then switched to doxycycline to complete 7 day course on ___. Likely has large component of venous stasis, so also recommend TEDs stockings and/or leg elevation. Right foot does still have triangular shaped area of erythema, but it does not look cellulitic or infected and pulses are full. Recommend continued observation. # Aortic stenosis: Previously moderate, now severe by echo on ___. The patient's cardiologist Dr. ___ was contacted with these results and recommended conservative management with tight control of blood pressure and fluid status. He is not a surgical candidate given his advanced age and comorbidities. # Vomiting: has known GERD, likely cause of epigastric discomfort. No vomiting since first day of admission (spit food out, not vomit per nursing). LFTs and lipase wnl, no evidence of pancreatitis or hepatobiliary disease. Video swallowing study was within normal limits. He was continued on home ranitidine and maalox PRN, and his symptoms resolved. # Atrial fibrillation: CHADS2 score of 3. Rate was well controlled this admission with home doses of digoxin, diltiazem, and metoprolol. His anticoagulation with warfarin was transiently held for 2 days, then restarted at previous reported dose of 2.5 mg daily. His INR has been only 1.1, however, for the last 3 days of his hospitalization, so he will need to have continued INR monitoring and adjustment of warfarin by the ___ MD at rehab to ensure that he reaches therapeutic INR again. # Acute renal failure: Cr on admission bumped to 1.2 from recent baseline 0.8-0.9, BUN also increased. Likely pre-renal in setting of decreased PO intake vs poor forward flow from CHF exacerbation and AS. He returned to baseline Cr with diuresis and remained stable for the duration of his hospitalization # Hyponatremia: chronic, remained within his baseline 128-133, likely hypervolemic hyponatremia ___ CHF. # Polypharmacy: patient has an extensive medication list of nearly 30 medications, many of which seems extraneous/unnecessary for a person of his age. He asked his providers to pare down his list while he was an inpatient, but then very vehemently demanded that he continue to be given all his home medications, so in the end no changes were made. Would strongly suggest that his medications be continuously re-evaluated for necessity by his rehab facility and PCP upon ___. # Chronic pain: has pain in back and legs secondary to spinal stenosis and past injuries related to falls, as well as pain in bilateral shoulders from chronic rotator cuff tears. He was continued on his home medication regimen. TRANSITION OF CARE ISSUES: - CHF: needs daily weights and assessment of pulmonary symptoms. If weight increases more than 3 lbs, or if he is having worsening shortness of breath or orthopnea, please call his cardiology NP ___ ___ to discuss appropriate medication changes - Anticoagulation: Will discharge on warfarin 2.5mg daily, but will need continued INR monitoring and warfarin dosing adjustment at rehab for his atrial fibrillation. Next INR should be on ___ and results communicated to ___ MD at rehab. - Foot erythema: has triangular area of erythema on right forefoot, does not appear to be infected. Has completed 7 day course of vancomycin then doxycycline.
